A1.justification: Both PDFs describe E2H Reasoner and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–J. Retained and newly added material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original reasoning and planning experiments across five benchmarks, with additional sample-efficiency, SFT, and scheduling analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds DAPO comparisons, AIME24/OlympiadBench evaluation, and training diagnostics.

M1.justification: v3 adds an E2H+DAPO variant whose difficulty-conditioned sampling feeds DAPO's filtering/resampling (Section 4.3). The cosine/Gaussian schedulers remain unchanged. The revised four-level description aligns with v2's existing experiments rather than establishing a new curriculum.

E1.justification: Table 7 adds AIME24 and OlympiadBench evaluation of MATH-trained models. This substantially extends transfer testing to separate challenging problem distributions beyond v2's five benchmarks and within-dataset difficulty/OOD splits.

E2.justification: Tables 5–6 introduce DAPO as an evaluated comparator across all five retained benchmarks, comparing baseline and E2H-scheduled variants under GRPO and DAPO. Earlier CoT, CL, Self-Evolve, and SFT comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce GRPO/DAPO scheduling controls and pass@1/pass@32 transfer evaluation of MATH-trained models. New preprocessing descriptions specify 1-shot CoT and fixed error-rate intervals, conflicting with retained zero-shot/quartile descriptions. These reported discrepancies do not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Tables 5–6 add ablations testing whether E2H complements DAPO. Appendix G.4 and Figure 7 additionally examine whether scheduling reduces zero-advantage batches during training. Existing decomposition, Gaussian-parameter, split-count, and SFT analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging across three seeds in Appendix E.2. New Figure 7 contains shaded bands, but their meaning and construction are unspecified, preventing a reliable determination of whether statistical uncertainty reporting changed.

E6.justification: Matched existing tables retain their scores, while v3 adds substantial DAPO, transfer, and training-trajectory results. For example, Table 5 reports Countdown OOD scores of 10.9 for DAPO and 30.1 for DAPO+E2H-G; Table 7 reports Qwen 1.5B AIME24 pass@32 of 10.0 for GRPO and 16.7 for E2H-G. These are new comparisons, not improvements to v2 runs.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 and Appendix A retain the same definitions, assumptions, convergence guarantees, sample-complexity results, and proofs. Their mathematical content is unchanged after accounting for pagination and whitespace.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: probabilistic easy-to-hard scheduling, improved reasoning/generalization, and conditional convergence and sample-efficiency guarantees. Added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix G.4 newly interpret E2H and DAPO as complementary, linking fewer zero-advantage batches to difficulty matching the model's competence. v3 also adds discussion of Self-Evolve's tuning burden. Appendix I's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds prompt and in-context-example sources, explicit difficulty-bin boundaries, and a DAPO default of n=4. Hardware, training duration, existing hyperparameter tables, decoding settings, and code access remain unchanged. The reward description is relocated rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for DAPO, Tajwar et al.'s curriculum-related work, Hao et al.'s prompting resources, AIME, and OlympiadBench. It extends positioning toward complementarity with DAPO while retaining the broader related-work narrative.

P1.justification: Localized revisions clarify task partitioning and expand experimental discussion, with new Appendix E.3 and G.4 subsections. Correspondence information changes and acknowledgments disappear, but the overall narrative and section organization remain.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 5–7 and Figure 7, refines captions for Figures 2, 5, and 6, and rearranges appendix floats. Existing diagrams and table structures largely persist; v2 Tables 5–13 correspond to v3 Tables 8–16.

improvement.justification: DAPO comparisons and AIME24/OlympiadBench transfer tests strengthen empirical support, while Figure 7 adds a useful training diagnostic. These gains are tempered by contradictory difficulty-split descriptions and undefined plotted bands. The revision provides a limited net improvement without resolving those reproducibility gaps.
